home.sub: Satellites measure the ocean's temperature around Roatán, Utila, Guanaja and Cayos Cochinos every day. Here you can see how much heat has built up, from 1985 to today, and explore the reefs in 3D.
home.mapLabel: Map of the Bay Islands with today's heat stress
home.cardsLead: Average of the 5 km cells around each island. Degree heating weeks (°C-weeks) add up the extra heat of the last 12 weeks.
home.stripesTitle: Forty years of heat, island by island
home.stripesLead: Each stripe is one year, colored by the highest heat stress that island had.
home.caveat: These are satellite measurements of the ocean surface in 5 km cells: a regional signal, not a measurement on any one reef.
alert.building.desc: Heat building up: risk of possible bleaching.
alert.a2.desc: Risk of reef-wide bleaching with death of heat-sensitive corals.
alert.a4.desc: Risk of severe, multi-species mortality (over 50% of corals).
alert.a5.desc: Risk of near-complete mortality (over 80% of corals).
heat.kicker: NOAA Coral Reef Watch, 1985 to today
heat.title: Heat stress by island
heat.lead: NOAA publishes ocean heat for the whole planet, but not island by island. Here we compute it for each island group from the daily 5 km satellite grid.
heat.chartLead: Heat built up day by day around each island. The shaded band is bleaching season (August to October).
scene.hover: Move the cursor over the island to see its data.
scene.exaggeration: Relief exaggerated ×4; depths beyond 40 m compressed.
scene.modelNote: Satellite-based model; not a navigation chart.
scene.depthModel: Shallow depths estimated from reef zones (satellite bathymetry pending).
scene.heatNote: Each square is one 5 km satellite cell: a regional signal, not a measurement on a reef.
scene.noWebgl: Your device can't show 3D. You can see each island's data under Heat stress.
scene.modelSoon: 3D model of a real coral: coming soon.

about.lead: ReefQuest is free and nonprofit. Everything you see comes from open data, processed by us and stored on this site. This is how it works and where its limits are.
about.caveatsTitle: What these data can and can't tell you
nowebgl.title: Your device can't show 3D

footer.made: Made in Honduras for the islands' schools, communities and divers.
footer.free: Free, nonprofit and built on open data.
scene.hint: Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom, and drag with two fingers (or right-click) to rotate. Tap the dots to read their stories.
boat.title: Research vessel R/V Arrecife
boat.heading: Heading
boat.mission: Mission: make a CTD cast over every habitat in this zone.
boat.missionDone: Mission complete: you logged every habitat in the zone.
boat.aground: Shallow water! Back up or tap deeper water.
boat.hintTouch: Tap the water to sail · drag to look around
boat.hintKeys: W A S D or arrows to sail · click the water to go there · space: cast the CTD · U: underwater

home.title: Ocean heat, seen from space
home.fig1Title: Today's heat stress across the Bay Islands
home.fig1Sub: Degree heating weeks in 5 km satellite cells, {date}.
home.fig1Caption: Each square is one 5 km cell of NOAA's product, colored by the heat built up over the last 12 weeks; from 4 °C-weeks, bleaching is expected. Lines are depth contours. Tap an island to open it.
home.fig1Source: Source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch v3.1 (5 km). Depth and mainland coast: GEBCO 2023. Islands: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Chart: ReefQuest.
home.tableNote: The dotted line in the small charts marks 4 °C-weeks (Alert 1).
heat.source: Source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch v3.1 (5 km), data through {date}. Island averages: ReefQuest.
heat.recordLead: The three years with the most heat stress on each island. Tap a row to show it in the figure.
heat.scaleLead: NOAA extended the scale in 2023 with three new levels for extreme events.

scene.timebarKey: Each stripe is one year, colored by its heat peak. Tap one to jump to that year.
boat.zonesLead: Sail a research vessel over the reef, map the seafloor and take samples.
scene.layer.habitat.what: Colors of the Allen Coral Atlas satellite classification, instead of the natural view.
scene.layer.heat.what: Heat built up in NOAA 5 km cells, on the date below.
scene.layer.contours.what: Depth every 5 m over the reef; every 200 m offshore.
scene.aboutData: About the data and its limits
scene.guide1: Move around. Drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom; two fingers or right-click to rotate.
scene.guide2: Read the seafloor. Under the water you see pale sand, dark seagrass and the reef; the foam marks the crest where waves break. Turn on “Habitat map” to see the satellite classification.
scene.guide3: Watch the heat. The bar at the bottom is time. Tap a year or press ▶ to see the heat that bleaches corals build up.
scene.guide4: Open the stories. The coral diamonds tell what happened at each place; from some you can head out on the research vessel.
home.reliefCredit: Seafloor relief: GEBCO 2023 depth contours, 20 to 3,000 m.
